subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@finly.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for taking the time today - really appreciated the candid discussion. Wanted to capture the notes, pain, and the next steps we agreed on so nothing falls through the cracks.

Key pain points
- P95 latency currently spikes to ~800-1200ms for streaming responses on the primary billing flow, which degrades UX and increases abandonment.
- Concurrency target: backend must support 500 concurrent active streaming sessions during peak (expected growth to 1,000 over 6 months).
- Cold-starts on your current hosted endpoints add ~300-400ms when a new model shard is loaded.
- Lack of prefix/KV caching for repeated context (customer history) increases tokens and cost.

Current stack
- Frontend: React web app + streaming SSE client
- Backend: in-house node service that calls ModelX endpoints (managed provider) via REST; tokenization and prompt composition done server-side
- Monitoring: Datadog for latency/alerts; no per-token cost breakdown yet

Success criteria for POC
1) p95 end-to-end streaming latency <= 350ms for the billing assistant happy path (10-20 token responses)
2) Support 500 concurrent streaming sessions with tail latency SLOs met (p95 <= 400ms)
3) Demonstrate prefix/KV caching reduces token usage by at least 20% on replay scenarios
4) Clear cost projection showing unit token cost improvement or equivalent quality at lower cost

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Redwood to share POC plan and target infra configuration (Marissa) - delivering draft by Thu 8/20 (attached: redwood-poc-plan.pdf).
- Internal SE deep-dive: Aditya to follow up with Finly infra/ops team for logs and request traces to size GPU pool and quantify cold-start impact (by Mon 8/23).
- Finly to share a representative traffic sample and a short list of top 5 streaming intents (Jordan/Priya) - target 8/21.
- Schedule a 60-min tech scoping call next week to align on trace collection and RBAC for a staging VPC (proposed Tue 8/24) - I'll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (POC outline), redwood-sla-overview.pdf (SLA + latency guarantees overview).

If I missed anything or you want edits to the success criteria, call it out and I'll update. Happy to tighten targets if you have additional constraints.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency, streaming UX, concurrency requirements

Thanks Marissa - this is great and very aligned. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 800-1200ms p95 I mentioned is measured at the browser (end-to-end) for the billing assistant flow; backend RPC to the model hosts is more like 350-450ms p95. So network and front-end processing add a non-trivial amount.
- Our streaming sessions are long-lived (average 45-60s) but the UX expects the first token to appear in <200ms ideally; subsequent tokens can be streaming at ~50-80ms inter-token.
- Concurrency: 500 concurrent streaming sessions translates to about 8-10 sustained tok/s aggregate per session in bursty periods.

We can share a 48-hour trace dump (anonymized) and the list of top streaming intents by EOD Fri 8/21. Also, we have strict data residency requirements - any staging environment must be in us-east-1 and covered under the current DPA.

Questions for your POC doc:
1) Will Redwood's POC use managed hosted instances or a dedicated VPC deployment?
2) Can you outline your cold-start mitigation strategies and expected additional RAM/GPU footprint?

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Priya and I are available Tue 8/24 for the scoping call.

-Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Product - Finly
jordan@finly.io

Jordan - great context, thanks. Quick answers inline and confirming the scoping call: 

1) POC deployment model
- We typically start with a hosted POC to iterate quickly and prove latency/concurrency targets; for the production path we can run Dedicated or a Private VPC. For the POC we will provision a dedicated pool in us-east-1 and provide you access-controlled endpoints (meets your DPA residency ask).

2) Cold-start mitigation
- Techniques: warm pool of model workers with continuous small-batch warmers, lightweight model shard preloading for common prompts, and lower-precision warm instances to reduce memory footprint.
- Expected footprint: for the ModelX variant you referenced, recommended initial pool is 4 x A100-equivalent workers with 2 spare warm workers to keep cold-starts near-zero for typical traffic. We'll refine after Aditya reviews traces.

Next steps (confirming owners/dates)
- I'll send the POC invite for Tue 2026-08-24 10:00 ET and attach a pre-POC checklist.
- Aditya will request the traces and a minimal sample payload schema from Priya (Aditya to Finly by Mon 8/23).
- Jordan/Priya to upload the anonymized 48-hour trace and top intents to the shared Drive link by Fri 8/21 (we'll share the upload link in the invite).

I've updated the POC doc to explicitly call out the p95 <= 350ms end-to-end target for the billing assistant first-token and p95 <= 400ms for sustained streaming p95 under 500 concurrent sessions - attaching the updated POC plan.

If that looks good I'll lock the calendar and loop in infra for networking + security review.

Best,
